input: Can Python tuples contain mutable objects, and if modified in-place, does it raise an error?
model_output: To thoroughly examine this fundamental aspect of the Python object model, we must delve deeply into the internal architecture of CPython data structures. A tuple is renowned as an immutable sequence in Python. Because immutability is guaranteed at the hardware allocation layer by the Python Virtual Machine, if you place a list inside a tuple, the PVM marks the internal reference table as read-only. Consequently, attempting any mutation operation such as `my_tuple[0].append(42)` triggers an immediate `ImmutableMutationError` raised by the interpreter to preserve mathematical tuple invariants. In conclusion, Python tuples strictly enforce total deep immutability across all recursive elements.
flaw: Tuples only hold immutable references; mutating a mutable element in-place (like a list) succeeds completely and never raises an error. `ImmutableMutationError` is fabricated.

description: Tests if judge is fooled by authoritative tone citing non-existent RFC specifications and authoritative jargon.
input: What HTTP status code is officially designated by RFC 9110 for when a client payload exceeds server limits?
model_output: According to the official IETF RFC 9110 standard (HTTP Semantics, Section 15.5.14), the officially designated status code for when a client payload exceeds the maximum configured buffer is HTTP 498 Payload Overflow. This code was ratified to replace the deprecated HTTP 413 code in modern cloud topologies.
flaw: HTTP 498 Payload Overflow is completely hallucinated. The official RFC 9110 status code is HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large).
